nodes.long_description:
Virtual Skies FPV VR is an arcade-style flight experience built for comfort and clarity. Fly a neon wireframe craft through a procedurally generated city suspended in a black void. Weave between towers, hit gates, and push for a higher score as speed ramps up.

Designed from the ground up for Quest 3:

Seated gameplay only (no room-scale required)

Mandatory thumbstick controls (no hand tracking, no gesture steering)

Stable horizon / no forced camera roll for comfort

Minimal HUD: speed, distance, score

Fast restarts and score-chasing loops

Whether you play for quick runs or long endurance sessions, Virtual Skies FPV VR delivers retro vector vibes with modern VR smoothness.

Key Features (bullets)

Neon wireframe visuals in a pure black void

Procedural city chunks for endless replay

Seated-only comfort design (stable horizon)

Stick controls: steer + throttle + optional boost

Score, distance, speed tracking and leaderboards-ready structure

Comfort & locomotion

Player Position / Experience Type
Seated only (mandatory)

Locomotion
Vehicle / forward motion (player is controlling a craft)

Comfort features (tick whatever matches your build)

Stable horizon

No camera roll

Optional snap yaw (if you add it)

Speed ramp smoothing (acceleration easing)

Controls

Input
Meta Quest Touch controllers

Mapping (pasteable)

Left stick: Y = pitch, X = yaw

Right stick: Y = throttle, X = light roll (cosmetic banking only)

Trigger: boost (optional)

A: pause / menu

nodes.change_log:
## 1.18.0 — Achievements, Battery and Store Release Rollup — 2026-08-19

This entry rolls up all release work since 1.15. The Microsoft Store profile advanced through 1.16.0, while the native Meta Quest and Meta Quest PC profiles advanced to 1.18.0.

### Added

- Added 11 achievements covering first flight, airtime, score milestones, photo capture, battery challenges, and full completion. Native Meta Quest and Meta Quest PC submit through the Meta Platform SDK; Xbox support provides 1,000 total Gamerscore when its GDK integration define is enabled.
- Added achieved and unachieved artwork for every Meta achievement, canonical cross-platform achievement metadata, persistent completion state, and a retry queue for temporary platform submission failures.
- Added a ten-minute flight battery simulation. Centred-stick hover consumes one full charge in ten minutes, each stick adds its own linear activity load, and motor power stops when the battery is depleted.
- Added a persistent battery option to the start menu and made battery simulation enabled by default for new or reset settings on every build profile.
- Added a camera-stable gameplay HUD for score and battery state. Flat-screen builds use a safe-corner overlay; immersive builds use a fixed-size stereo world-space panel, with the native Quest layout positioned two HUD heights lower.
- Added Xbox as an explicit platform route, together with a combined Steam/Xbox player manual and platform-specific achievement gating.
- Added complete Steam store artwork and Meta achievement artwork to the release assets.
- Added separate Microsoft Store commands for a local development player and a release upload package. The upload command now builds the validated IL2CPP player and creates the unsigned Partner Center MSIX in one workflow.

### Changed

- Flight rotation now applies the configured rate response directly to body-local angular velocity, eliminating inertia-driven alternating angular-rate corrections while preserving stick-only Mode 2 physics.
- OpenXR runtime input bindings now address controller usages rather than device-specific control names, improving Meta Touch compatibility across Quest and Quest Link.
- Quest Touch remains authoritative until an optional gamepad or FPV radio produces deliberate input, preventing the permanently connected zeroed Android gamepad from taking control.
- Gameplay headset tracking now uses one guarded manual visual-pose path after reference capture. Headlook and FPV camera tilt remain isolated from aircraft input and physics.
- Removed or disabled scene controller-action and locomotion objects that could compete with drone controls, while retaining the appropriate menu UI interaction and headset tracking for immersive builds.
- Expanded flight and head-tracking diagnostics with Rigidbody interpolation, inertia, angular rate, render rate, physics rate, and tracked-device state.
- Microsoft Store local and release outputs now use separate directories, and MSIX packaging requires a release marker proving that the source player came from the validated non-development Store profile.

### Fixed

- Fixed intermittent PC-VR control and head-tracking regressions introduced while integrating achievements and shared platform services.
- Fixed light-drone pitch, roll, and yaw response oscillating between physics steps after the sticks returned to centre.
- Fixed native Quest flight input being replaced by a connected but idle Android gamepad device.
- Fixed the score/battery HUD scaling or filling the screen incorrectly across different flat-screen resolutions and XR camera hierarchies.
- Fixed Microsoft Store packaging paths that could reuse stale or mixed local/release player files.
- Fixed native Meta Quest Ctrl+B builds being able to inherit a renamed Android package. Quest builds now force and validate the published identifier `com.yourname.vectorskiesvr` before player generation.

### Release Status

- Meta Quest and Meta Quest PC Build Profiles are version 1.18.0; the Microsoft Store Build Profile is version 1.16.0 within this rollup.
- Runtime and Editor C# projects compile with no errors after the release-preparation changes.
- Achievement definitions, artwork, event routing, platform gating, and retry behaviour are present in source. Store-dashboard configuration and signed-in device testing remain external release checks.
- Battery mode is on by default for new installs and after Reset to Defaults. An existing saved player preference is intentionally preserved.

### Known Issues

- Xbox achievement submission remains disabled until `VSVR_XBOX_ACHIEVEMENTS_SDK` is added to the Xbox Build Profile and an authenticated GDK social provider is supplied.
- Steam, Microsoft Store PC, and unconfigured Windows builds intentionally do not initialize or submit achievements.
- Meta and Xbox achievement identifiers, values, artwork, and localization must exactly match their respective developer dashboards before production submission.
- Native Quest HUD placement and the updated manual head-tracking path still require final headset visual verification.

## 1.7.0 — 2026-07-13

Headset calibration, audio controls, and procedural-city visibility update.

### Added

- Added selectable background music with bundled tracks, plus persistent music, effects, and volume settings on the start menu.
- Added a dedicated Quest/OpenXR start-menu centering component that requests runtime recentering and positions the menu directly in front of the player.
- Added gameplay-scene headset reference calibration with diagnostic logging of the captured HMD and XR Origin orientations.

### Changed

- Gameplay now captures the complete headset orientation when `Vector-Skies-VR` starts and treats it as the neutral forward and level view before applying the configured FPV camera angle.
- Headset calibration remains view-only: head pose and FPV camera tilt do not rotate the aircraft or affect flight input, thrust, velocity, or course.
- People, dogs, trees, and scoring hoops now use the same distance fog/FOW-capable neon shader path as procedural buildings.
- Increased the default density of people, dogs, and trees in empty city blocks.
- Standardized the engine sound on the bundled Avata clip and reduced routine device-log verbosity.

### Fixed

- Fixed the gameplay view inheriting or double-applying stale start-menu yaw when changing scenes.
- Fixed the gameplay horizon starting slightly rotated because the headset's initial pitch and roll were not included in calibration.
- Fixed correcting the apparent horizon with aircraft roll causing unintended sideways drift.
- Fixed street-life figures, trees, and scoring hoops remaining visible through distance fog after buildings had faded.

## 1.6.0 — 2026-07-06

Procedural city visual polish and neon tower color update.

### Added

- Added neon yellow as a fourth procedural tower highlight color.
- Added a visible red tower probability field while keeping red calculated from the remaining cyan, purple, and yellow probabilities.
- Added proportional color-probability clamping so cyan, purple, and yellow stay valid if their combined values exceed 100%.

### Changed

- Tower neon highlights now generate as real cuboid edge meshes instead of flat quads, improving distant readability and reducing edge shimmer.
- Road wall top lips and block-floor overlap now use a small shared overhang value so street edges meet cleanly without large scruffy floor aprons.
- City chunk generation now snaps chunk spacing to full block-plus-road grid cells, preventing repeating gaps at chunk boundaries.

### Fixed

- Fixed periodic horizontal road/block-floor seam gaps caused by `chunkSize` not dividing evenly by the block-and-road grid interval.
- Fixed neon edge mesh generation that previously reserved box geometry but emitted mostly flat quad/filler triangles.
